text: When you join a session, you follow the host's coding agent live, at your own pace. Here is what you can see.
The first time you join, SpecDeck asks how you want to follow sessions.
Overview shows the documents and the timeline: what was asked, and what the agent did, in plain words.
Developer shows the host's terminal, next to every tool call, command and diff.
In Overview, each step is one line, such as Looked at one file, or Changed two files, marked as done, failed or running.
When Claude asks the host a question, you see the options, and which one the host chose.
Permission prompts are marked as allowed or denied by the host.
A line at the bottom says what the agent is doing right now, and for how long.
Change this any time with the layout button at the top: Overview, Developer, or Present for sharing your screen. Plain words or Every step sets how much each step shows. Nobody else's view changes.
The terminal is read-only. New output keeps arriving without moving your view, so you can scroll back at your own pace.
Command F, or Control F on Windows and Linux, searches the terminal and the timeline together.
Under Code, Files lists every file the agent changed. Select one to open its changes in a tab.
The bar at the bottom shows the model, the git branch, how full the context is, and the host's usage limits.
Everything you scroll, search or open changes only your own view.
